Unit 8: Describing Quantitative Findings

单元八：描述量化研究结果

Student Version | Course Notes & Statistical Analysis Tasks

学生版 | 课堂笔记与统计分析任务

Professional Workplace Communication: Proposal and Report Writing (LAN4103)

专业职场沟通：提案及报告写作（LAN4103）
Vocabulary: objectively (adverb): considering only facts and without being influenced by personal feelings or opinions

Learning Objectives

学习目标

By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

学完本单元后，你将能够：
  • identify the purposes of various visuals for presenting IT statistical data
  • describe quantitative findings (distributions, pre- and post-project comparisons, changes and trends)
  • select and describe salient findings clearly and objectively in evaluation reports
识别各种视觉图表在呈报IT统计数据中的用途 | 描述量化研究结果（分布情况、项目前后比较、变化和趋势） | 在评估报告中清晰客观地选取和描述显著发现

Quantitative findings are the numerical data collected using tools such as questionnaire surveys. They are expressed in numbers, percentages, or statistics, and provide measurable evidence to assess a project's effectiveness objectively. Visuals help people see comparisons, relationships, or trends clearly.

量化研究结果是使用问卷调查等工具收集的数值数据，以数字、百分比或统计数据表示，提供可量化的证据以客观评估项目成效。视觉图表有助于人们清晰地看到比较、关系或趋势。

Task 1: Presenting Statistical Data

任务一：呈报统计数据

Match each visual type to its appropriate purpose:

将每种视觉图表与其适当用途配对：
Visual TypeAppropriate Purpose (Match A–E)
1. Pie chart
2. Bar chart
3. Line graph
4. Table
5. Pictogram

Task 2a: Describing Distributions

任务二a：描述分布情况
Sample Formula: [General description] + [Segment description] + [Conjunction] + [Numerical description] + [Segment description]
Example: "More than half of the respondents checked their online systems for potential threats on a weekly basis, whereas 16% of them did so monthly."
描述饼图或百分比分布时，可将数字描述（如60%）与概括描述（如「超过半数受访者」）结合使用。

Reporting Grammatical Adjustments:

报告时的语法调整：
  • 'you' → 'respondents' / 'participants'
  • 'check' → 'checked' (simple past tense)
  • 'your' → 'their'
  • 'did so' to avoid repeating the full phrase

Practice 1:

Survey: "How often do you run anti-virus scans?"

Daily: 55% | Twice weekly: 37% | Weekly: 8% | Never: 0%

Practice 2:

Survey: "How often do you review website security certificates?"

Very often: 97% | Quite often: 3% | Occasionally: 0%

Task 2b: Describing Pre- and Post-Project Findings

任务二b：描述项目前后的结果
Example 1: "More than half of the respondents checked their online systems for potential threats on a weekly basis, which was a significant improvement from only 2% before the project."
Example 2: "About one-third of them did so every two weeks, compared to 10% prior to the project."
项目前后数据通过比较干预前后的态度或习惯来衡量影响。

Practice 1:

"How often do you test the firewall configuration?"

Once a month: Pre 0% → Post 5% | Once in three months: Pre 5% → Post 60% | Once in six months: Pre 10% → Post 25% | Never: Pre 85% → Post 10%

Practice 2:

"Do you agree that regular password resets are necessary to prevent data leakage?"

Disagree: Pre 96% → Post 0% | Somewhat agree: Pre 4% → Post 60% | Strongly agree: Pre 0% → Post 40%

Practice 3:

"Are you satisfied with the performance of the new AI agent?"

Very satisfied: Pre 7% → Post 75% | Satisfied: Pre 30% → Post 20% | Not satisfied: Pre 63% → Post 5%

Task 2c: Describing Changes and Trends

任务二c：描述变化和趋势
Trend Analysis Examples:
• "The percentage of clients who agreed that the prices of anti-virus software products were fair rose sharply from 23% two years ago to 77% this year."
• "The percentage of shoppers who thought the interface of our online store was poor fell remarkably from 97% to 17%."
• "The percentage of customers who wanted more product tutorials remained stable over the past three years (45% → 46% → 45%)."
• Contrast: "The number of respondents who ran anti-virus scans 'quite often' increased sharply from 5% to 90%, while those running scans 'occasionally' dropped significantly from 95% to 7%."
趋势分析范例：使用上升/下降动词（如rise、drop）搭配程度副词（如sharply、remarkably）来描述变化。用contrast连接词（如while、whereas）对比不同趋势。

Task 3: Reporting Salient Findings

任务三：报告显著发现
Vocabulary: salient (adjective): most important; noticeable or prominent

It is not necessary to report every detail. Select only the most salient findings to keep your evaluation focused and impactful. Highlight key changes such as a significant rise or decline, or major contrasts that demonstrate project impact.

无需报告每个细节。只选取最重要的研究结果，使评估聚焦且有影响力。突出显示关键变化，如显著的上升或下降，或展示项目影响的重大对比。

Case Scenarios — Identify the salient findings:

i. Challenges faced in adopting VR tools: [Lack of staff training] and [Limited integration with existing systems], accounting for the overwhelming majority of obstacles.

ii. Firewall implementation across 4 office networks (Security attacks Pre vs Post):

Office A: 17 → 16 | Office B: 28 → 2 | Office C: 32 → 19 | Office D: 47 → 47

iii. IDS deployment across network segments (Cyber threats without vs with IDS):

Segment A: 46 → 37 | Segment B: 22 → 21 | Segment C: 18 → 0 | Segment D: 4 → 5

iv. Cloud collaboration tool staff logins across departments:

Sales: 53 | R&D: 104 | Finance: 131 | HR: 178

任务四：撰写评估报告（第二部分——量化研究结果）

Project: 'Data Analytics Basics for Nonprofits'

Survey Data:

  • Q1 Familiarity with data analytics tools: Very familiar (Pre 12% → Post 26%), Familiar (Pre 5% → Post 68%), Quite familiar (Pre 10% → Post 6%), Not at all (Pre 73% → Post 0%)
  • Q2 Confidence in creating basic data visualisations: Highly confident (Pre 5% → Post 15%), Fairly confident (Pre 15% → Post 80%), Not at all (Pre 80% → Post 5%)

Unit 9: Describing Qualitative Findings

单元九：描述质性研究结果

Professional Workplace Communication: Proposal and Report Writing (LAN4103)

专业职场沟通：提案及报告写作（LAN4103）
Vocabulary: qualitative (adjective): relating to what something is like or how good it is, rather than how much of it there is

While quantitative data provides measurable evidence of an IT project's outcomes, qualitative data reveals the reasons and user perspectives behind system adoption and performance. Reporting qualitative findings complements metrics with human insights.

量化数据提供项目成果的可量化证据，而质性数据（意见、开放式回答、访谈）则揭示数据背后的原因和洞察。你将学习报告质性研究结果，以人文视角补充数据驱动的结果。

Task 1: Analysing Qualitative Data (Categorisation)

任务一：分析质性数据（分类）

Classify each comment as Positive, Negative, or Irrelevant based on tone and relevance to the 'CyberSecure HK' project:

根据语气和与「CyberSecure HK」项目的相关性，将每条评论分类为正面、负面或无关：

A. 'The hands-on practice with real-world scenarios was incredibly helpful.'

B. 'Absolutely disappointed! No advanced tools are covered in the workshops.'

C. 'The real-world scenarios about phishing are so relatable.'

D. 'The examples provided were highly relevant to my daily work.'

E. 'No support outside the workshops! I feel completely abandoned!'

F. 'I love the cybersecurity tools introduced. They are all very useful.'

G. 'I have to push back my schedule just to attend the workshop.'

H. 'I had to park my car far away from the training centre.'

Task 2: Reporting Positive Comments

任务二：报告正面评价
Three-Step Thematic Process:
1. Group comments into common themes → 2. Identify significant themes → 3. Summarise and report key insights
三步主题分析法：1. 将评论归类为主题；2. 识别重要主题；3. 总结并报告关键洞察。

Key Themes Identified from Focus Group:

  • Theme 1: High relevance of real-world cybersecurity scenarios (e.g. phishing simulations)
  • Theme 2: Practical utility of security tools (e.g. two-factor authentication)

Reporting Key Insights using Reported Speech:

a. Real-world scenarios: "It was commented that the real-world phishing scenarios were highly relevant to participants' daily work."

b. Security tools: "Some participants were satisfied with the usefulness of the cybersecurity tools, noting that two-factor authentication effectively enhanced device protection."

Task 2b: Practice — Reporting VR Workshop Comments

任务二b：练习——报告VR体验工作坊评价

1. 'The workshop was really engaging! The immersive VR experience is truly transformative.'

2. 'I am interested in learning more about VR technology.'

3. 'The instructor clearly explained how the VR works and the step-by-step guidance is easy to understand.'

Task 3: Reporting Negative Comments Tactfully

任务三：委婉报告负面评价
To provide a balanced evaluation, negative comments must be reported to pinpoint areas for improvement. Use neutral, professional, and constructive language rather than harsh or critical wording.
为提供平衡的评估，必须报告负面评论以指出改进领域。使用中立、专业和建设性的语言，而非严厉或批评性的措辞。

Comparison:

  • Harsh: "No support outside the workshops! I feel completely abandoned!"
  • Version A (Direct): "Some expressed that there was no support outside the workshops. They felt completely abandoned."
  • Version B (Tactful & Constructive): "Some thought the learning process would be more effective with additional support outside the workshops."

Techniques:

TechniqueDirect / Rude FeedbackTactful Reporting
1. Replace rude/offensive words with neutral terms'The course fees are a complete RIP-OFF!'Some students thought that the digital audio production course fees were somewhat high.
2. Focus on the issue, not the person'The instructor spoke so fast; I couldn't follow the steps.'Feedback indicated that the instruction pace was quite fast, making certain technical steps difficult to follow.
3. Use frequency words to show non-constant issues'If I can't book a digital audio workstation through the online system, how am I supposed to practise?'It was reported that users occasionally experienced difficulties booking digital audio workstations through the online system.
4. Highlight constructive elements'The front desk was a disaster! The staff were so rude when I asked about schedules!'Feedback revealed that customer service communication at the front desk could be improved.

Task 3c: Practice — Rewriting Negative VR Comments Tactfully

任务三c：练习——委婉改写VR体验负面评价

1. 'We waited too long for our turn to try on the VR headsets.'

2. 'The handouts were poorly written and didn't match what we were taught in the workshop.'

3. 'The VR headset kept crashing, which made the training pointless and confusing!'

Task 4: Completing an Evaluation Report (Part III — Qualitative Findings)

任务四：完成评估报告（第三部分——质性研究结果）
CA Assessment: This task mirrors the EAII exam format. Draft Section 3 (cont'd) incorporating qualitative feedback tactfully.
此任务模拟EAII考试格式。请巧妙地将质性反馈纳入报告第三部分（续）。

Focus Group Feedback from 'Data Analytics Basics for Nonprofits':

  • Positive: 'The real-world dataset exercises are highly practical and easy to understand. Fantastic! 😊'
  • Constructive: 'My device was too outdated for running the data analytical tools, so the hands-on exercises were quite frustrating. 🙁'
  • Negative (Emotional): 'Totally IRRELEVANT! No non-profit data or examples? What a complete waste of time! 😡'

3. Findings (cont'd) — Qualitative Feedback

Task 1: Mobile Game Development Basics

任务一：手机游戏开发基础
You are Angel Chan, a project assistant at InnoTech Education Institute. You have conducted a mini-project to teach teenagers foundational skills in mobile game design and programming through hands-on workshops. You are required to write an evaluation report to your supervisor discussing the effectiveness of the project and giving recommendations for the way forward. Using the notes and data you have compiled, complete the evaluation report with appropriate elaboration.
你是InnoTech Education Institute的项目助理Angel Chan。你开展了一个迷你项目，通过实践工作坊教授青少年手机游戏设计和编程的基础技能。你需要向主管撰写评估报告，讨论项目成效并提出改进建议。

Evaluation report on the 'Mobile Game Development Basics' project

1. Introduction

The booming mobile gaming industry has sparked teenagers' interest in game development. Despite this growing enthusiasm, many lack the technical knowledge and creative skills needed to design functional and engaging games. The objective of the 'Mobile Game Development Basics' project is to teach teenagers foundational skills in game design, programming, and problem-solving through hands-on workshops. This report assesses the effectiveness of the project and provides suggestions for future improvement.

蓬勃发展的手机游戏行业激发了青少年对游戏开发的兴趣。尽管热情高涨，但许多人缺乏设计功能性和吸引力游戏所需的技术知识和创意技能。「手机游戏开发基础」项目的目标是通过实践工作坊教授青少年游戏设计、编程和问题解决的基础技能。本报告评估项目成效并为未来改进提供建议。

2. Methodology

2.1 Participants

Three professional game developers were recruited as trainers, while 40 teenagers from various secondary schools in Hong Kong were invited to participate in the project.

三名专业游戏开发者获聘为培训师，40名来自香港各中学的青少年受邀参加项目。

2.2 Implementation

From January to February 202-, five workshops were conducted by the trainers. These sessions covered topics such as coding basics using the Unity game engine, designing user interfaces, implementing game mechanics, and testing functionality. Participants engaged in practical exercises, including prototyping simple games and troubleshooting common issues.

一月至二月期间，培训师举办了五节工作坊。课程涵盖使用Unity游戏引擎的编程基础、用户界面设计、游戏机制实现和功能测试等主题。参与者进行了实践练习，包括制作简单游戏原型和排除常见问题。

2.3 Evaluation

To evaluate the project, participants had been invited to complete a pre-project survey in December 202- assessing their prior knowledge of game development. In March 202-, a post-project survey was administered, and online group discussions were held to gather feedback on their experiences and challenges faced during the workshops.

为评估项目，参与者于十二月完成了评估其游戏开发先验知识的项目前调查。三月进行了项目后调查，并举办了线上小组讨论以收集他们在工作坊期间的体验和挑战反馈。

Evaluation Report on 'Cantonese for All' Project

1. Introduction

The non-Chinese speaking (NCS) students who are new to Hong Kong often face challenges in integrating due to language barriers. The mini-project, 'Cantonese for All', aims to help these students learn Cantonese to improve their daily interactions and community integration. This report discusses the effectiveness of the project and provides recommendations for future initiatives.

新来的非华语学生因语言障碍往往面临融入社区的挑战。「人人学广东话」迷你项目旨在帮助这些学生学习广东话，改善日常交流和社区融合。本报告讨论项目成效并为未来活动提供建议。

2. Methodology

2.1 Participants

Two instructors were recruited to deliver the course, while 50 new NCS students from Hong Kong Higher Institute were invited to participate in the course.

两名导师获聘授课，50名来自香港专上学院的新非华语学生受邀参加课程。

2.2 Implementation

From October to November 202-, twelve 1-hour lessons were conducted by the instructors. These lessons focused on teaching the NCS students useful daily Cantonese expressions, such as greetings, ordering food, and asking for directions, in addition to some highlights of local culture.

十月至十一月期间，导师共举办了十二节一小时的课程。课程重点教授非华语学生实用的日常广东话表达，如问候、点餐和问路，同时介绍本地文化亮点。

2.3 Evaluation

To collect data for evaluation, the NCS students completed a pre-project survey in September 202-. In December, they took part in a post-project survey and focus group interviews to share their experiences.

为收集评估数据，非华语学生于九月完成了项目前调查。十二月，他们参加了项目后调查和焦点小组访谈，分享他们的体验。

  1. Findings
  2. Discussion
  3. Conclusion
  4. Recommendations

In view of the positive findings, it is recommended that monthly workshops be offered so that more hotel staff will benefit from them, while previous staff will have opportunities to refresh their knowledge and practise their Korean. Meanwhile, it is advisable to develop and provide supplementary online materials, such as video tutorials and interactive exercises, enabling staff to reinforce their skills at their own pace. To offer authentic conversation practice, it is suggested that additional sessions with native Korean speakers through virtual platforms could be organised.
鉴于积极的研究结果，建议每月举办工作坊，让更多酒店员工受益，同时让之前参加的员工有机会温习知识并练习韩语。同时，建议开发并提供补充网上材料，如视频教程和互动练习，让员工按自己的步伐巩固技能。为提供真实的会话练习，建议透过虚拟平台增设与母语为韩语人士的环节。

Evaluation Report on ‘Impact and Success of V-Music Library’ Project

「V-Music Library的影响与成效」项目评估报告

1. Introduction 简介

Music education and industry exposure are vital for nurturing young musicians. However, many students lack access to platforms that connect them with professionals and audiences. This mini-project, ‘Impact and Success of V-Music Library’, aims to assess how effectively the V-Music Library initiative supports music education, fosters collaboration, and promotes student creations. This report aims to discuss the effectiveness of the project and gives recommendations for the way forward.

音乐教育及业界接触对培育年轻音乐人至关重要。然而，许多学生缺乏接触专业人士和观众的平台。迷你项目「V-Music Library的影响与成效」旨在评估V-Music Library计划在支持音乐教育、促进协作及推广学生创作方面的成效。本报告旨在讨论项目成效并提出未来发展建议。

Completed Parts of the Report (2/2)

报告已完成部分

2. Methodology 研究方法

2.1 Participants 参与者

Six students were recruited as researchers, while 40 HKDI students and alumni participated in surveys, interviews, and workshops.

六名学生被招募为研究员，40名HKDI学生及校友参与调查、访谈及工作坊。

2.2 Implementation 实施

From October to November 202-, the researchers attended vinyl record workshops, observed mini-concerts, and interviewed participants and staff involved in the V-Music Library. They also analysed visitor engagement during the “Timeless Ideas & Icons” exhibition.

202-年10月至11月，研究员参加了黑胶唱片工作坊、观察迷你音乐会，并访问了参与V-Music Library的参加者及职员。他们亦分析了「Timeless Ideas & Icons」展览期间的访客参与情况。

2.3 Evaluation 评估

To collect data for evaluation, the students and alumni had been invited to take part in a pre-project survey in September 202-. In December, a post-project survey was administered and focus group interviews were arranged for participants to share their experiences.

为收集评估数据，学生及校友受邀于202-年9月参加项目前调查。12月进行了项目后调查，并安排焦点小组访谈，让参与者分享他们的体验。

参考回应

3. Findings 研究结果

After the project, nearly 70% of the respondents reported that they felt slightly confident in using digital music tools such as DAWs and samplers, showing a considerable rise from only 22% who expressed similar confidence before it. Likewise, the percentage of respondents who reported lacking confidence fell sharply from 64% before the project to just 2% after its completion. Moreover, three quarters of the respondents reported feeling motivated to work with other musicians after the project, showing a significant increase from only 5% prior to it. Notably, just 2% remained hesitant to collaborate, marking a substantial improvement from the previous 80%.

项目结束后，近70%的受访者表示他们对使用DAW和采样器等数字音乐工具稍有信心，较项目前仅22%表达类似信心有相当大的上升。同样，表示缺乏信心的受访者百分比由项目前的64%大幅下降至项目结束后的仅2%。此外，四分之三的受访者表示在项目后有动力与其他音乐人合作，较项目前仅5%有显著增加。值得注意的是，仅2%仍对合作有所犹豫，较之前的80%有大幅改善。

It was commented that the library offered rare vinyls that inspired new composition styles. However, some respondents said that there were not enough networking opportunities with producers and artists. In addition, they suggested that the library interface could be made more user-friendly and easier to navigate.

有人评论指，图书馆提供的珍稀黑胶唱片启发了新的作曲风格。然而，一些受访者表示，与制作人和艺人交流的机会不足。此外，他们建议图书馆界面可以更用户友好、更易于浏览。

Possible Response (2/3)

参考回应

4. Discussion 讨论

The findings suggest that the V-Music Library has successfully enhanced students’ confidence in using digital music tools such as DAWs and sampler, which are essential in modern music production. Moreover, the collaborative features of the V-Music Library have encouraged peer-to-peer learning and strengthened connections between students and industry professionals, fostering a more engaging and supportive educational environment.

研究结果显示，V-Music Library成功提升了学生使用DAW和采样器等数字音乐工具的信心，而这些工具对现代音乐制作至关重要。此外，V-Music Library的协作功能促进了同侪学习，并加强了学生与业界专业人士之间的联系，营造了更具吸引力和支持性的教育环境。

5. Conclusion 结论

To conclude, the project has been successful in helping students and alumni acquire practical music production skills and build collaborative networks. While it is obvious that we should continue with this meaningful initiative, some areas for improvement have been identified to achieve better outcomes.

总括而言，该项目成功帮助学生及校友掌握实用的音乐制作技能并建立合作网络。尽管我们显然应继续推行这项有意义的计划，但已发现一些需要改进的地方，以取得更好的成果。

Possible Response (3/3)

参考回应

6. Recommendations 建议

In light of the positive outcomes, it is recommended that regular tutorials and artist interviews be introduced so that students can deepen their understanding of music production and gain insights from industry professionals. Moreover, it is advisable that networking events and webinars with music producers and artists be arranged to allow participants to build connections and explore collaboration opportunities. To further improve the effectiveness of the V-Music Library, it is suggested that the interface be redesigned and simplified in order that users can navigate the platform more easily and make full use of its resources.

鉴于积极的成果，建议引入定期教程和艺人访谈，让学生加深对音乐制作的理解，并从业界专业人士身上获得启发。此外，建议安排与音乐制作人和艺人的交流活动及网络研讨会，让参与者建立联系并探索合作机会。为进一步提升V-Music Library的成效，建议重新设计并简化界面，使用户能更轻松地浏览平台并充分利用其资源。

1. Introduction 简介

The AdTech Festival was designed to engage the public in exploring the future of advertising technologies. The mini-project, AdTech Festival: Future of Advertising, aims to raise public awareness of advertising technologies. This report discusses the effectiveness of the project and provides recommendations for future initiatives.

AdTech Festival旨在吸引公众探索广告科技的未来。迷你项目「AdTech Festival：广告的未来」旨在提高公众对广告科技的认识。本报告讨论项目成效，并为未来的活动提出建议。

2. Methodology 研究方法

2.1 Participants 参与者

The festival involved industry experts, creative professionals, and over 200 public attendees. The sessions were held at HKDI Gallery over three days.

节庆活动汇聚了业界专家、创意专业人士及200多名公众参加者。活动在HKDI Gallery举行，为期三天。

2.2 Implementation 实施

From October to November 202-, the project was executed in three phases: content curation and speaker invitations, venue setup and promotional campaigns, and the festival itself, which included interactive exhibits, expert talks, and post-event media coverage.

202-年10月至11月期间，项目分三个阶段执行：内容策划及邀请讲者、场地布置及宣传推广，以及节庆活动本身，包括互动展品、专家讲座及活动后的媒体报道。

2.3 Evaluation 评估

To collect data for evaluation, the participants had been invited to take part in a pre-project survey in September 202-. In December, a post-project survey was administered and focus group interviews were arranged for participants to share their experiences.

3. Findings 研究结果

After the project, 62% of respondents reported that they were familiar with advertising technologies such as AR and AI, compared to approximately one-fifth prior to the project. Slightly more than a quarter stated that they were highly familiar, representing a significant increase from the mere 3% who had reported a high level of familiarity before the project. Additionally, the vast majority of participants (93%) reported feeling inspired to explore creative advertising tools, with more than three-quarters describing their level of inspiration as very high after the project.

项目结束后，62%的受访者表示他们熟悉AR和AI等广告科技，而项目前约为五分之一。略多于四分之一的人表示非常熟悉，较项目前仅3%表示高度熟悉有显著增加。此外，绝大多数参与者（93%）表示受到启发去探索创意广告工具，其中超过四分之三的人表示启发程度在项目后非常高。

It was commented that the AR demo was amazing and helped participants learn more about immersive branding. However, some respondents said that certain exhibits were too technical for beginners. A few mentioned that the expert talks could be more accessible, as technical jargon occasionally hindered engagement.

有人评论指，AR演示非常精彩，帮助参与者更深入了解沉浸式品牌。然而，一些受访者表示部分展品对初学者来说过于专业。少数人提到专家讲座可以更易理解，因为专业术语偶尔会妨碍参与。

Suggested Answer (2/3)

建议答案

4. Discussion 讨论

The findings suggest that cutting-edge advertising tools have effectively enhanced public awareness of emerging technologies. AR demos, AI-generated content, and interactive exhibits provided hands-on experiences that not only enhanced engagement and learning but also encouraged deeper exploration of the showcased innovations.

研究结果显示，尖端广告工具有效提升了公众对新兴科技的认识。AR演示、AI生成内容及互动展品提供了亲身体验，不但提升了参与度和学习成效，还鼓励参加者更深入探索所展示的创新科技。

5. Conclusion 结论

To conclude, the project has been successful in enhancing public understanding and interest in advertising technologies. While the project met its core objectives, some areas for improvement have been identified to achieve better outcomes

总括而言，该项目成功提升了公众对广告科技的理解和兴趣。尽管项目达到了核心目标，但已发现一些需要改进的地方，以取得更好的成果。

Suggested Answer (3/3)

建议答案

6. Recommendations 建议

In view of the positive outcomes, it is recommended that future festivals include beginner-friendly guides and interactive tutorials so that attendees with varying levels of expertise can benefit equally. Moreover, it is advisable that multilingual support and simplified content be provided to accommodate diverse audiences. To further improve the effectiveness of the project, it is suggested that expert talks be accompanied by visual aids and glossary handouts in order that participants can better follow the discussions and reduce confusion caused by technical jargon.

鉴于积极的成果，建议未来的节庆活动加入初学者友好的指南和互动教程，让不同程度的参加者都能同样受益。此外，建议提供多语言支持和简化内容，以照顾不同的受众。为进一步提升项目成效，建议专家讲座配以视觉辅助工具和词汇表讲义，让参加者更易理解讨论内容，并减少因专业术语造成的困惑。

Evaluation Report: 1. Introduction

评估报告：1. 引言

Evaluation report on ‘Data Analytics Basics for Nonprofits’ project

「非营利机构数据分析基础」项目评估报告

As the importance of data analytics continues to grow in today’s data-centric world, many local non-profit organisations in Hong Kong find themselves lacking the necessary skills to harness data for organisational growth. This mini-project, ‘Data Analytics Basics for Nonprofits’, sets out to improve their understanding of data analytics and provide them with practical skills by introducing basic analytical tools and techniques. This report evaluates the project’s effectiveness and offers recommendations for future enhancements.

随着数据分析在当今以数据为本的世界中日益重要，香港不少本地非营利机构发现自己缺乏善用数据以推动机构发展所需的技能。这个小型项目「非营利机构数据分析基础」旨在通过介绍基础分析工具和技巧，加深他们对数据分析的理解，并为他们提供实用技能。本报告评估项目的成效，并就日后的改进提出建议。
The highlighted parts show the key information you will reuse in the Discussion, Conclusion and Recommendations.
高亮部分是你在讨论、结论及建议部分将会再用到的关键信息。

Evaluation Report: 2. Methodology

评估报告：2. 研究方法

2.1 Participants

2.1 参加者

Four IT students were recruited as instructors, while 25 local non-profit organisations were invited to join the project.

招募了四名IT学生担任导师，并邀请25家本地非营利机构参加项目。

2.2 Implementation

2.2 实施

From January to February 202-, five online workshops were conducted by the instructors, during which they demonstrated how to use spreadsheet functions, interpret simple data visualisations, and apply basic statistical methods. Participants also engaged in hands-on exercises using real datasets.

于202-年一月至二月，导师举办了五场网上工作坊，示范如何使用电子表格函数、解读简单的数据可视化图表及应用基本统计方法。参加者亦参与了使用真实数据集的实践练习。

2.3 Evaluation

2.3 评估

To gather evaluation data, participants were asked to complete a pre-project survey in December 202- on data analytics and visualisation. In March 202-, a post-project survey was conducted, and virtual focus group discussions were held to collect feedback and review participants’ experiences.

为收集评估数据，参加者于202-年十二月须完成一份关于数据分析及可视化的项目前问卷调查。202-年三月进行了项目后问卷调查，并举行了网上焦点小组讨论，以收集反馈及回顾参加者的体验。

3.1 Quantitative Findings: Data Sources & Analysis

3.1 量化研究结果：数据来源及分析

Pedagogical Analysis

教学分析
  • General Numerical Expressions: Rather than merely reporting raw percentages, the output uses academic approximations (‘slightly more than two-thirds’ for 68% at (1); ‘approximately a quarter’ for 26% at (4)), as the template prompts.
    一般数字表达：不只是列出原始百分比，而是运用学术性的约数表达（68%写成“略多于三分之二”，26%写成“约四分之一”），符合模板提示。
  • Template Stems Followed Strictly: Each sentence keeps the template’s fixed stems (‘After the project…’, ‘compared to … before’, ‘Moreover, the number of respondents who…’, ‘while those … fell’); only the numbered blanks are filled, and trend words come from the template’s options (‘a significant increase’, ‘rose sharply’, ‘fell drastically’).
    严格沿用模板句式：每句均保留模板固定句式（“After the project…”、“compared to … before”、“Moreover, the number of respondents who…”、“while those … fell”），只填写有编号的空格；趋势用语取自模板选项（“a significant increase”、“rose sharply”、“fell drastically”）。
  • Reported Speech & Pronoun Cohesion: ‘said that they were…’ and ‘reported that they were very familiar with them’ use reported speech, and ‘them’ refers back to ‘data analytics tools’ to avoid repetition.
    转述句与代词衔接：“said that they were…”及“reported that they were very familiar with them”使用转述句，代词“them”指代“data analytics tools”，避免重复。

3.2 Qualitative Findings: Data Sources & Analysis

3.2 质性研究结果：数据来源及分析

Pedagogical Analysis

教学分析
  • Constructive Rephrasing of Raw Feedback: The raw comment at (15), ‘Totally IRRELEVANT! No non-profit data or examples? What a complete waste of time!’, is neutralised into ‘some of them suggested that more data and examples specific to non-profit organisations should be used’, following the teacher’s asterisk rule.
    把原始反馈改为建设性表达：(15)的原始评论为“完全不相关！没有非营利机构的数据或例子？简直浪费时间！”，按教师的星号规则中和为“部分受访者建议使用更多针对非营利机构的数据和例子”。
  • Diplomatic Problem Articulation: At (14), ‘quite frustrating’ becomes the formal ‘faced issues with outdated devices … which hindered their learning experience’.
    委婉地陈述问题：(14)中的“相当令人沮丧”改为正式表达“遇到设备过时的问题……影响了学习体验”。
  • Template Stems & Transition Markers: ‘It was also found that’, ‘However, some respondents mentioned that’ and ‘Furthermore, some of them suggested that’ introduce the positive point, the problem and the suggestion in turn.
    模板句式与过渡词：“It was also found that”、“However, some respondents mentioned that”及“Furthermore, some of them suggested that”依次引出正面意见、问题及建议。

Pedagogical Analysis

  • Expanding Short Meeting Notes: The notes ‘five workshops → boost knowledge & cultivate mindset’ and ‘improved skills → data-driven mindset fostered’ become a causal chain: workshops → tool skills → everyday behaviours (analysing data, spotting trends) → operational efficiency.

3.4 & 3.5 Data Sources & Analysis

3.4及3.5 数据来源及分析

Pedagogical Analysis: Problem–Solution Triad

教学分析：问题与对策三项配对

The three recommendations do not give generic advice; they map directly to the evidence:

三项建议并非泛泛而谈，而是直接对应实证数据：
  1. 1. Recommendation (21) capitalizes on the strong positive survey results (68% familiar, 80% confident) by institutionalizing recurring workshops and introducing peer mentoring.
    建议(21)善用积极的问卷结果（68%熟悉、80%有信心），将定期工作坊制度化并引入朋辈指导。
  2. 2. Recommendation (22) directly eliminates the hardware hurdle identified in Feedback (14) by establishing a pre-workshop IT readiness checklist and troubleshooting protocols.
    建议(22)针对反馈(14)指出的硬件障碍，设立工作坊前的IT准备清单及故障排除程序。
  3. 3. Recommendation (23) directly resolves the operational disconnect highlighted in Feedback (15) by mandating non-profit-specific case studies.
    建议(23)针对反馈(15)指出的与实际运作脱节问题，要求使用针对非营利机构的个案研究。

Language Focus

语言重点
  • Modal Verbs & Structures: ‘it is recommended that regular workshops could be offered’, ‘it is advisable that a checklist … should be provided’ and ‘we should use case studies …’ keep the template’s recommending stems.
